Dr. Elena Vasquez — Contact Dynamics and Slip Detection said about it: The 2014 Wettels Chapter.pdf (E31) states Pacinian corpuscles respond 60 to 500 hertz and detect slip vibration as small as 1 micrometer at 200 hertz center frequency, and that BioTac slip power resides in 100 to 500 hertz separable from slower contact events, which is why Dr.
Dr. Elena Vasquez — Contact Dynamics and Slip Detection said about it: The 2014 Wettels Chapter.pdf (E31) samples the alternating current, Alternating Current means the fast vibration part, pressure signal at 2200 hertz and decides in 30 millisecond total window as half the 60 to 80 millisecond human grip reflex time; the stick-to-slip simulation (E38) shows micro-slip at 53.6 milliseconds and gross slip at 96.8 milliseconds with stick ratio falling 0.95 to 0.48, so a 30 millisecond detector fits inside the 43.2 millisecond gap for Dr.
Manager said about it: The numbers that decide it are zero blocking objections on the board, 2200 Hz sampling with 30.0 ms window from the BioTac slip chapter (E31), 9.00 ms converter update in the converter datasheet (E41) and 51.2 kbit per s message rate (E52), so Dr.
